reason: Verified per-site (RFC 0106 wave 4g): `/\At\d+_r\d+\z/.match?(name)` (join_dependency.rb:121) is Rails' heuristic for "is this column one of the join aliases". trails already holds the exact alias set the aliases object emitted, so `instantiate` tests `aliasSet.has(key)` (join-dependency.ts:738) instead of re-deriving it from the alias spelling. Same partition of the result columns, no regex to match against.
